the experimental electron density of Ca(2+)–calmodulin (Ca(2+)-CalM) reveals extensive disorder, bound 2-methy-2,4 pentanediol and that the crystal structures of Ca(2)-CalM are biased towards more open conformations due to bound 2-metyl-2,4pentanediol.
extensive main-chain and side chain disorder and bound 1,2-methyl-1,2,4-pen-tanediol (2MPD) were revealed in a single-wavelength anomolous diffraction data set for Ca(2+)(CaM) at 1.0Å resolution.

the crystallographic structure of Ca(2+-CaM) has been determined to atomic resolution, and the structure reveals extensive disorder and a bound ligand, 2-methyl2,4-pen-tanediol, that was not previously known to be bound.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of high-resolution data and experimental electron-density maps can provide a more complete understanding of the structure and dynamics of Ca(2+) -CaM.

the combination of a high-resolution data set and density-modified electron-density map enabled the accurate characterization of the extensive disorder in Ca(2+)CaM and the assignment of bound MPD in the N-terminal binding pockets of this protein.

the combination of high-resolution experimental phase information and a robust automated model-building protocol enables the accurate modeling of extensive disorder, which is critical to understanding protein function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
experimental electron density is an invaluable resource for characterizing the disorder and bound molecules in macromolecular crystals.
the combination of high resolution and density modification can be used to reveal disorder in protein crystal structures.
the use of MPD to crystallize Ca(2+), Ca(2+)/CaM, and Ca(2+)/(CaM target protein) complexes is not recommended.
